# Fork delta: profiling-owned vendored files

Upstream: `nestjs/observe@7500fba` (see `PIN.md`; `LICENSE` is the verbatim upstream MIT text). Plan references:
`artifacts/01_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` sections 3.8, 4 and 7. Status: Mission 02 slice B (sampler POC). Every vendored file carries
the header `// Adapted from nestjs/observe@7500fba (MIT, Copyright (c) 2017-present Kamil Mysliwiec). Changes: see third_party/nestjs-observe/FORK_DELTA.profiling.md`.

| Tracelet file | Upstream file (pin) | Action | Changes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `src/profiling/vendor/fold-profile.ts` | `src/profiling/fold-profile.util.ts` | modify (substantial) | Removed: `SpanSlice` import, `slices` option, `findSlice`, per-span (`spanId`/`traceId`) tagging and the `startedAt` origin (no span attribution in v1; the profile is per instance and window). Output is now `FoldResult { stacks: {stack, samples}[], sampleCount, idleSampleCount, totalSampleCount, firstSampleUs, lastSampleUs }` with the stack already joined by `;` (contract `ProfileStack`). Added: `(idle)` leaf samples counted in `idleSampleCount` instead of silently skipped; first/last sample timestamp (`profile.startTime` + cumulative `timeDeltas`, idle included) for sample-based `gapBeforeMs`, coverage and `achievedSampleRateHz`; `achievedSampleRateHz()` helper; frame paths relative to `process.cwd()` with `file://` stripped through `fileURLToPath` (Windows safe) and forward slashes, non-file URLs such as `node:internal/...` kept; `;` inside a frame replaced by `,`; frame length cap 512; depth cap `maxFramesPerStack` (default 128): the 127 leaf-most frames behind a `(truncated)` root frame; stacks merged after truncation; deterministic ordering (samples desc, then text). Kept: `(program)` and `(garbage collector)` frames, `(root)` and `(idle)` dropped from stacks, 1-based line numbers, anonymous name `(anonymous)`, per-node stack built once |
| `src/profiling/vendor/cpu-sampler.ts` | `src/profiling/cpu-profiler.service.ts` | rewrite (shared idea only) | Removed: `CpuProfilerService` duty cycling (`dutyMs`, `windowTimer` + `dutyTimer`), a new `Session` per burst, `enforceBudget` / `maxCpuPercent` and the permanent `disable()` kill switch, `SpanSliceRecorder`, `process.cpuUsage()` budget. Added (plan 7, H1/R5/M8): ONE persistent `Session` connected once; `Profiler.enable` and `setSamplingInterval` once; one chained `setTimeout` loop (re-armed after each rotation, unref'd, armed in `runOutsideTrace`); every window `Profiler.stop` immediately followed by `Profiler.start` on the same session, bracketed by a rotation keep-alive (`RotationKeepAlive`, default `node:inspector`'s V8 `console.profile` / `profileEnd` with title `tracelet:rotation-keepalive`, opened just before the stop and closed just after the start) so the inspector's started-profile count never reaches 0 and V8 does not dispose and re-create the CpuProfiler (re-creation re-logs every code object with full heap walks, a stall proportional to heap size; M02 investigation), skipped silently when the inspector console is missing or `begin()` throws, disabled after a throwing `end()`, only defaulted together with the default session; folding moved to a `setImmediate` after the restart; separate `stopStallMs` / `startStallMs` / `foldMs`; `gapBeforeMs` from sample timestamps (first sample of this window minus last sample of the previous one), never from `startTime`/`endTime`; `pause()` / `resume()` for backoff (first window after resume has no gap); `stop()` flushes the partial window; injectable session factory and clocks; errors are reported through `onError` after tearing the session down |
| `src/profiling/inspector-probe.ts` | new | new | `v8_enable_inspector` flag, `process.getBuiltinModule('node:inspector')` (no top-level import, so a Node built without the inspector still loads the package) and a throwaway `Session.connect()` |
| `src/profiling/profile-mapper.ts` | new (replaces upload mapping in `profile-uploader.ts`) | new | `FoldResult` to the `CpuProfile` contract: top-K `maxStacksPerProfile`, then lowest-sample stacks trimmed until the estimated size is within `maxProfileBytes`; trimmed stacks go to `droppedStackCount`/`droppedSampleCount`; schema bound of 32768 chars per stack enforced |
| `src/profiling/profiler.service.ts` | new (lifecycle only; upstream `profile-uploader.ts`/uploading is not used) | new | State machine `starting/running/backoff/disabled/unavailable/stopped/error`, backoff (3 consecutive windows above `maxStallMs` -> pause 1, 2, 4, 8 windows, resume, reason names the dominant block), one retry after 60 s on an inspector error, hand-off of `ProfileItem` to the `TelemetryQueue` contract, `ProfilerHealthSource`, bounded debug ring of per-window records |

Not part of this slice (Mission 06): `vendor/runtime-metrics.ts`, `vendor/node-runtime-metrics.interface.ts`, `metrics-collector.ts`.
Not vendored on purpose: `span-slice-recorder.ts`, `profile-uploader.ts` (HTTP upload to the SaaS; Tracelet stores to MongoDB).

## Review-round additions (slice B hardening)

- **Keep-alive default (M1).** The rotation keep-alive (V8 console `profile`/`profileEnd`) is broadcast to every inspector session whose Profiler domain is enabled. It is therefore NOT used by default when `NODE_V8_COVERAGE` is set, when `--cpu-prof` or any `--cpu-prof-*` flag is in `process.execArgv` or `NODE_OPTIONS` (`keepAliveDisabledReason()`), or with an injected session. Opt-out is an internal/debug-only dependency (`createKeepAlive: null` on `ContinuousProfilerDeps` / `SamplerOptions`); `profiling.*` in the frozen config contract has no such field and was NOT changed. `ProfilerDebug.keepAlive` is `'active' | 'off' | 'failed'` (+ `keepAliveOffReason`); each `WindowRecord.keepAliveMs` is the begin+end cost (already inside stop/start stall). When the keep-alive cost dominates a backoff, the reason says another inspector session probably has the Profiler enabled.
- **Known interplay.** A second in-process session with the Profiler enabled (DevTools, Jest/vitest v8 coverage providers, a second Tracelet instance) makes `begin()` cost a heap walk (reviewer: 178 ms at 24 MB, 1.06-1.09 s at 589 MB). That cost is charged to `stopStallMs` and can trip backoff; it is visible in `keepAliveMs`.
- **Host `console.profile` (L6).** Because Tracelet's session keeps the Profiler enabled, a host calling the global `console.profile('x')` without a matching `profileEnd` leaves that profile open for the life of the process (it is recorded into Tracelet's CpuProfiler and keeps it alive, memory grows with the unterminated profile). Reviewer finding, not re-measured here beyond the design reading. Document in the README (Mission 06).
- **Unbudgeted costs (L2).** The initial `start()` and `resume()` after a backoff create a fresh CpuProfiler (full heap walks, heap-proportional: about 1.1 s at 550 MB). They are not part of the per-window `maxStallMs` budget; their cost is recorded in `ProfilerDebug.counters.lastInitialStartMs` / `lastResumeMs`.
- **Privacy (M2).** `fold-profile.ts` `sanitizeFramePath()`: frames inside `process.cwd()` are relative; anything else (other drive, UNC, posix absolute, `..`) becomes `node_modules/<pkg>/...` or `<external>/<basename>`; `node:` URLs are kept; other URL schemes are reduced to `<external>/<basename>` without query or credentials. No stored frame contains an absolute path, a drive letter, a backslash or the OS user name (unit tests and T09/T10 assertions).
- **Robustness.** A throwing `onWindow` consumer tears the sampler down before `onError`; an orderly `stop()` never reports an error or schedules a retry; the single error retry is restored after 10 healthy windows; negative raw sample gaps are counted (`counters.negativeGaps`).
